fields.title: Polka: eight seconds to the cart
fields.summary: 34% drop-off: people leave before the result appears. Total response time is 11.2 seconds.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do first? Name the price of your solution.
fields.brief/role: You are the PM for Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner dashboard.
fields.brief/context: You are the PM for Polka. The "build a weekly cart" feature is in beta. Drop-off is 34%: people leave before the result appears.
fields.brief/objective: Let the user see the result sooner instead of waiting for eleven seconds.
fields.brief/constraints: Beta runs every day. Reducing the catalog takes two weeks.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do first and name what remains.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: People leave not because the screen is slow, but because it is empty
fields.learnTakeaway/body: In an AI interface, what matters is not the total response time, but the moment the first sign of a result appears. Therefore, streaming usually delivers more than model acceleration, and the next battle is for time to first token: prompt part order, cacheable invariant part, absence of a polite preamble before what the user came for.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: Input 12,400 tokens (full store catalog), output 600. TTFT 3.2 s, speed 75 tokens/s. Total time 11.2 s.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: Spinner, then the entire answer at once. No streaming.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: Starts with an explanatory paragraph (about 90 tokens), then the product list.
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: "Streaming — 4 days. Catalog reduction to relevant via search — 2 weeks. Prompt caching — 3 days, but requires the invariant part to come first; currently the user profile is at the beginning."
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Four days. The answer is output as it generates rather than all at once at the end.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: total time does not change, first products appear in 3.2 s instead of 11.2. Based on data from other features, drop-off should drop about threefold. Does not touch TTFT of 3.2 s — the pause before the first token.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Catalog reduction via relevant search. 2 weeks.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: input drops from about 12,400 to 3,500, TTFT to about 1 s, cost drops threefold. Total time around 9 s — still too long without streaming.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Streaming plus caching plus format fix
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: Streaming plus caching plus format fix. 7 days.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: streaming provides perception, caching cuts TTFT roughly in half, removed preamble saves another second before the first product. First product in about 1.2 s.
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Three weeks. Streaming, prompt caching, format fix, and catalog reduction via relevant search — immediately and fully.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: best result in both time and cost. Three weeks with a 34% drop-off every day of the beta.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not distinguish between TTFT and total time
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not design the interface for generation
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not connect context volume to speed and cost
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Time to first token is not separated from total response time
